fixes.explanation: You've got it, friend. “When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.” (Judges 1:28) Israel got stronger and put the Canaanites to work. Then comes that little “but,” and it carries the whole verse. It's like me saying I'll clean out the junk drawer and then closing it with half the stuff still inside.

Big plans, baker, but the verse keeps its feet on the ground. Judges 1:28 says that when Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, “…but they never drove them out completely.” Every last one? NOT what it says. Israel got stronger, the Canaanites stayed, and that's the part to remember.

You caught it, baker. Judges 1:35 says, “But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.” The house of Joseph got stronger and the Amorites got put to work, but nobody got sent away. That's like moving the dough to the other side of the counter and calling the counter clean.

A cheer would sound nice, baker, but the text goes another way. When the angel finished speaking to all the Israelites, “…the people lifted up their voices and wept.” (Judges 2:4) I think this one is heavy. They raised their voices, and what came out was weeping.

A stone is a fair guess, friend, but this verse doesn't mention one. Judges 2:5 says, “So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.” They gave the place a name and brought sacrifices to the LORD right there. I'd say that's a good thing to do after all that weeping.
